title: Edition 1 (trial)
notes: Trial edition: the first Donna Daily website edition, ported from the Nov 1 trial Page with every source re-checked. More stories arrive with the twice-daily updates.

stories.headline: Last call: NYC early voting closes at 5 p.m. today; Election Day is Tuesday
stories.summary: Today is the ninth and final day of early voting in New York City, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., at your assigned early-voting site, which can differ from your Election Day site. On Tuesday, Nov 3, polls open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., and anyone in line by 9 p.m. can still vote. Mail and absentee ballots must be postmarked or dropped off by Nov 3. Nationally, Reuters reports more than 51 million Americans had already voted, citing the University of Florida Election Lab, up from about 46 million before Election Day in 2022.
stories.why: All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot, deciding whether Republicans keep control of Congress (they hold the Senate 53-47).
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Judge bars DOJ from pressuring election officials over ballots; administration appeals
stories.summary: A federal judge on Friday ordered the Trump administration not to threaten or coerce state and local election workers into halting the processing of ballots from voters it alleges are ineligible. The order runs through Nov 16. The Justice Department appealed to the 9th Circuit on Saturday. Separately, federal prosecutors are investigating whether aides to Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola recruited a candidate whose name resembles Sen. Dan Sullivan's; Peltola's campaign and that candidate deny it.
stories.why: Fights over who gets counted could shape close races and post-election challenges.
stories.label: Fact + allegation
stories.note: The noncitizen-voter claims and the Alaska recruitment claim are allegations, not proven.

stories.headline: Judge throws out Trump's defamation suit against WSJ over Epstein letter story
stories.summary: A federal judge in Miami, Darrin Gayles, dismissed Trump's amended defamation suit against Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal with prejudice, meaning it cannot be refiled. The judge found Trump again failed to plausibly allege the paper acted with actual malice in its July 2025 story about a birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein. Trump, who denies writing the letter, plans to appeal.
stories.why: It is a major test of how far a sitting president can push libel suits against the press.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: D.C. and Virginia sue to stop Trump's triumphal arch at Memorial Circle
stories.summary: Virginia and the District of Columbia filed a federal lawsuit to block a triumphal arch the administration plans to start building as soon as Nov 5. Their suit argues the arch lacks the required approval from Congress, would exceed D.C.'s 130-foot height limit, and skips environmental and historic-preservation reviews.
stories.why: The ruling will decide whether a major new monument goes up at one of Washington's most visible gateways.
stories.label: Allegation
stories.note: Claims are the plaintiffs' legal arguments; no court has ruled yet.

stories.headline: Sweden's Almgren wins NYC Marathon in his debut; Chepkirui takes women's title
stories.summary: Andreas Almgren pulled away from Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa in the last mile to win in 2:06:01, the third-fastest time in the course's history. Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race in 2:24:36 for her second NYC title, and American Jessica McClain finished second.
stories.why: A first-time marathoner winning New York is rare; the last to do it was in 2010.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Bank of Canada raises its key rate to 2.5%, its first hike in three years
stories.summary: The Bank of Canada lifted its policy rate a quarter point to 2.5%, citing high oil prices that could spread into broader inflation. Governor Tiff Macklem said another hike is possible but the bank will decide one meeting at a time.
stories.why: Higher rates mean pricier mortgages and loans for Canadians; the next decision is Dec 9.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Ottawa takes up to a C$1.6B stake in Toronto AI firm Cohere
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a federal equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere as part of a large funding round alongside private investors. The Globe and Mail reports the round values Cohere at C$35.7 billion. Carney said the deal keeps the company Canadian.
stories.why: It is an unusually direct government bet on a homegrown AI company in a costly, unprofitable industry.
stories.label: Fact
stories.note: The exact ownership percentage was not disclosed.

stories.headline: Canada and the EU launch an 'Alliance for the Future' and talk closer membership
stories.summary: At a Canada-EU summit, the two sides announced a new alliance on areas including AI, energy and critical minerals, open to other like-minded countries. Canada is pursuing a new 'associate' relationship with the EU, with talks aiming to wrap up by June 2027.
stories.why: Canada is building ties beyond the US as trade with Washington stays turbulent.
stories.label: Fact
stories.note: What 'associate membership' would mean legally is still undefined.

stories.headline: Argonauts knocked out of CFL playoffs; Lions beat Roughriders in the West
stories.summary: Winnipeg beat Toronto 25-22 in the Eastern Semi-Final on Halloween. Argos quarterback Chad Kelly told TSN he felt his throwing shoulder 'separating' in the second half and expects a 4-6 week recovery. In the Western Semi-Final, Nathan Rourke threw for 366 yards and three touchdowns as BC beat Saskatchewan 33-26.
stories.why: Toronto's season is over, and Winnipeg and BC move on to the division finals on the road to the Grey Cup.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Workers rally at Vancouver airport against Ottawa's privatization plan
stories.summary: Unionized federal workers rallied at YVR against Ottawa's plan to let private investors run the country's four largest airports under long-term concessions while the government keeps the land. Union leaders argue it could cut wages and services.
stories.why: The plan could change how Toronto Pearson, Vancouver and other big airports are run and priced.
stories.label: Fact + opinion
stories.note: Warnings about cuts are the unions' view.

stories.headline: Tai Po fire report faults inspectors; housing chief Winnie Ho resigns
stories.summary: Hong Kong released the independent committee's report on last November's Wang Fuk Court fire, which killed 168 people. It heavily faulted the Housing Bureau's inspection unit. Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned to take political responsibility, and leader John Lee and officials bowed in apology. Some survivors told HKFP the apology lacked sincerity.
stories.why: It is the city's deadliest fire in decades, and the findings drive sweeping building-safety reforms.
stories.label: Fact + opinion
stories.note: The released report is redacted; criminal cases over the fire are ongoing.

sources.title: Report of Independent Committee released

stories.headline: Hong Kong moves to make renovation bid-rigging a crime and scraps disgraced inspection unit
stories.summary: The government proposed making bid-rigging, price-fixing and similar collusion in building-repair tenders a criminal offence with up to 10 years in jail. It also said the faulted inspection unit will be replaced within about a month by a new section, with its roughly 300 staff moving over.
stories.why: Triad-linked bid-rigging in renovations was flagged by the fire inquiry as a serious problem.
stories.label: Fact (proposal)
stories.note: The criminal offence is a proposal; RTHK reports the target is to pass it by April.

stories.headline: Eight firms, including Uber and Didi, apply for Hong Kong's first ride-hailing licences
stories.summary: The Transport Department received eight applications before Friday's deadline under the city's new ride-hailing rules. Uber, Tada, Amap and Didi confirmed they applied, and the first approvals are expected in late November or early December.
stories.why: Ride-hailing has operated in a legal grey zone in Hong Kong for years.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Hong Kong just had its warmest October since records began in 1884
stories.summary: The Observatory said October's mean temperature was 27.6°C, with the average high and low also setting October records. It blamed a very strong El Niño and a weak northeast monsoon, with climate change also playing a role. A cooler monsoon is expected early this week.
stories.why: Record heat is becoming routine, even in what is normally a mild month.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: About 15,000 run the first Northern Metropolis Marathon, in the heat
stories.summary: The inaugural race ran from Shek Mun through Tai Po and the Lung Shan Tunnel to the new Fanling Bypass. Runners said the heat was tough and some complained about too few water stations. Organizers hope to hold future races in cooler months and may extend the route toward Shenzhen.
stories.why: It showcases the government's huge Northern Metropolis development zone.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: China's factories shrank again in October, the third contraction in four months
stories.summary: The official manufacturing index fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September; below 50 means contraction. Reuters reports weaker demand at home and cooling export orders, and economists urged more support for growth.
stories.why: Exports have carried China's economy this year, and that engine is showing strain.
stories.label: Fact + analysis
stories.note: Calls for more stimulus are economists' views.

stories.headline: China's Zhang Haiqin wins 53kg gold at home weightlifting worlds by one kilogram
stories.summary: At the IWF World Championships in Ningbo, Zhang totalled 221kg (98kg snatch, 123kg clean and jerk) to edge American Miranda Ulrey's 220kg. A final 126kg lift that would have broken the world standard failed. North Korea's Kim So Hyon took bronze.
stories.why: It is a home-soil world title in a new Olympic weight class at the start of the Los Angeles 2028 cycle.
stories.label: Fact (state media)
stories.note: Reported by Xinhua; not independently corroborated here.

stories.headline: China steps up patrols east of Taiwan and around Scarborough Shoal
stories.summary: China's coast guard said it ran law-enforcement patrols in waters east of Taiwan on Saturday, part of a rise in activity there since June. A day earlier, the military and coast guard patrolled around Scarborough Shoal, calling it a response to Philippine 'provocations' without giving details.
stories.why: Taiwanese officials say they believe China is rehearsing a possible blockade.
stories.label: Fact + allegation
stories.note: Blockade practice is Taiwan officials' assessment; Beijing calls the patrols routine.

stories.headline: Shenzhen tightens security and bans drones ahead of APEC summit
stories.summary: Guangdong police are stepping up security, including drone bans, before the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, where Xi and Trump are expected to meet. In October the SCMP reported, citing unnamed sources, that US and Chinese negotiators were racing to finish investment deals before then.
stories.why: The summit is the next big moment for the US-China trade truce.
stories.label: Fact + reported
stories.note: Deal talks are based on unnamed sources (SCMP, Oct 20; may be paywalled).

stories.summary: State broadcaster CGTN reports the year's box office, including presales, has topped 31.5 billion yuan, and highlights a push to pair films with sports events to drive spending.
stories.why: Cinema is a key test of whether Chinese consumers are spending again.

stories.headline: Iran holds talks via Qatar as region braces for possible US strikes after the midterms
stories.summary: Iranian envoys met Qatari mediators in Doha on Saturday on ways to end the Gulf war, Reuters reported, citing a source. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump hasn't decided on new strikes and prefers diplomacy. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces to respond immediately and without geographic limits to any attack.
stories.why: A return to fighting could hit oil prices and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.label: Fact + analysis
stories.note: Talks details come from one anonymous source.

stories.headline: Canelo Alvarez regains WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh
stories.summary: Mexico's Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez, 36, beat France's previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision (115-112, 116-111, 117-110) in his first fight since losing to Terence Crawford in September 2025. AFP notes the bout went ahead despite Houthi drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia that have called off other events.
stories.why: Boxing's biggest star is back as a champion, and the fight shows Saudi Arabia keeping big events going despite the conflict.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Spain's deadliest high-speed rail crash kills 69; probe focuses on control center
stories.summary: A Renfe high-speed train slammed into a stopped Iryo train near Urda, south of Madrid, on Wednesday, killing at least 69 people. Investigators are looking at how the control center responded after a safety signaling system failed on the Madrid-Seville line.
stories.why: It raises questions about safety on one of Europe's busiest high-speed networks.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Oleshky civilians reach Ukraine under a rare truce as Russian strikes cut power
stories.summary: Exhausted residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky crossed into Ukraine under a six-day local ceasefire mediated by US first lady Melania Trump with the Pope's involvement, after a long trip via Crimea, Russia and Belarus. Meanwhile, Russian strikes left tens of thousands without power, including in Kyiv.
stories.why: It is the first humanitarian truce of its kind in more than four years of war.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Mayon volcano erupts in the Philippines; 2,000+ evacuated
stories.summary: A moderately explosive eruption on Oct 30 sent ash 3 km high and put Mayon on Alert Level 3. More than 2,000 people were evacuated, and about 420 families spent All Saints' Day in evacuation centers.
stories.why: Mayon is the Philippines' most active volcano, and a bigger eruption would force more evacuations.
stories.label: Fact
